name: Swamp Fox Passage Dispersed Primitive Camping - Francis Marion National Forest

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Francis Marion District

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required for general forest dispersed camping
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 30-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted throughout general national forest lands outside developed fee areas. Campsites set back 100ft from trails and water bodies.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6 inches deep in sandy soil, 200 feet from swamps and streams. Pack out toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace pack-it-in pack-it-out.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Clear pine straw 10 feet around fire ring. Extinguish cold to touch.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Obey South Carolina Forestry Commission burn bans.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved state highway changing to unpaved gravel forest roads (FS 204 / FS 212)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Flat gravel forest roads; low spots can turn muddy after heavy coastal rainstorms.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Normal low clearance front wheel drive car (accessible on main gravel forest roads in dry weather)

nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low (Flat Atlantic coastal plain pine flatwoods)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 65-80°F, pleasant coastal climate, blooming azaleas and dogwood.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot and humid (90-95°F), high mosquito / yellow fly activity, afternoon downpours.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Ideal camping season (65-78°F daytime, 45-55°F nights), low rain.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Mild coastal winter (55-65°F daytime, 38-45°F nights), premier winter boondocking.

dangers_and_hazards: Venomous snakes: Copperheads, Cottonmouths, and Eastern Diamondback Rattlesnakes active in warm months
Mosquitoes and ticks near cypress swamps

common_human_made_sounds: Occasional passing car on US-17 / SC-45

human_demographics_and_culture: Palmetto Trail backpackers, winter vanlifers, coastal kayakers, and local hunters.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Santi and Sewee indigenous traditions revere the coastal cypress swamps and pine flatwoods of Francis Marion as sacred spirit lands.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Peaceful coastal pine savannah grounding energy, gentle winter climate, rich history.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: Winding boardwalks and dirt paths through coastal pine flatwoods and cypress swamps

public_reviews_summary: Excellent free winter primitive camping destination in South Carolina. Flat, quiet pine woods with dependable cell service.
other_data: Bortle Class 3 night sky. Great solar panel output.

name: Chattooga River Corridor Dispersed Primitive Camping

management_agency.name: US Forest Service - Sumter National Forest (Andrew Pickens Ranger District)

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - USFS Wild & Scenic River Primitive Camping (zero fee)
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted along Chattooga Wild & Scenic River corridor. Camp 50ft minimum from river and 50ft from trails.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Dig cat-hole 6-8 inches deep in organic soil 200 feet from Chattooga River. Pack out hygiene products.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Dead and down wood gathering permitted on site.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in established rock fire rings only. Fully extinguish with water before departing.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved SC Hwy 28 to gravel Forest Service roads (FR 711 / Burrells Ford Road)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Paved state highway main access, graded gravel forest roads.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Accessible by standard 2WD low clearance passenger cars.

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 3-4 bars 4G LTE along SC Hwy 28 ridge pullouts
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Moderate inside deep river gorge; high on surrounding ridges

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 58-75°F, roaring waterfall flows, blooming mountain laurel.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: 75-88°F, prime river swimming & whitewater kayaking weather.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: 52-72°F, vibrant Blue Ridge Escarpment autumn foliage.

dangers_and_hazards: Fast river rapids and deep hydraulic pools in Chattooga River

acoustic_environment.quietness_rating: 9/10 - Roaring river rapids and forest wind

human_demographics_and_culture: Cherokee ancestral land (Keowee territory), whitewater kayakers, South Carolina backpackers, nomads.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Traditional Cherokee lands honoring the sacred Chattooga ('He who has crossed the river') as a sacred lifegiving river.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Powerful Wild & Scenic river energy, roaring waterfall thunder, pristine mountain solitude.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: King Creek Falls, Spoonauger Falls, river gorge bluffs

public_reviews_summary: Unmatched Wild & Scenic river primitive camping in South Carolina. Emerald river pools, roaring waterfalls, fast cell internet near Walhalla, and 100% free USFS access.
other_data: Sumter National Forest. Free primitive dispersed camping.
